findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the 'ticket dirs' gotcha in the Approach: what the phrase is, whether it triggers, and which rule keeps it from being accepted (parallel to the 'bug surfaced' explanation).
evidence: Testing: "the acceptor-arm gotchas ('bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept ...)"
Approach explains 'bug surfaced' ('surfaced' excluded from verb set) but contains no mention of 'ticket dirs' or its mechanism
findings.finding: AC4 and Testing require the 'ticket dirs' gotcha to NOT be accepted, but the Approach never defines what the 'ticket dirs' case is or why it would reach/trip the acceptor, unlike the 'bug surfaced' FP which is fully explained.
scenarios: Executor writes the detector's acceptor logic and cannot tell what token/prose 'ticket dirs' represents or which rule suppresses it
The unit test for 'ticket dirs' cannot be authored deterministically without knowing the intended trigger/accept path
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence in the acceptor section describing the 'ticket dirs' case (e.g. the substring 'ticket dir' resembling a ticket-id citation but not matching the hex-grouped/word-triple id shapes, so it must fail the acceptor) mirroring the 'bug surfaced' rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a detector unit test asserting denylisted hex-like tokens (ed25519, sha256, and any other denylist entries) do NOT trigger the SHA-like-hex arm.
evidence: Approach: 'SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc)'
Testing lists only acceptor-arm gotchas: "'bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases MUST accept, escape hatch honored"
AC4 enumerates FP gotchas but not the hex denylist entries
ABSENCE: no named test that ed25519/sha256 (or other denylisted hex-like tokens) stay green
findings.finding: The detector's SHA-like-hex trigger arm carries a denylist ('ed25519/sha256 etc') to suppress false positives, but the Testing section names no test asserting these denylisted tokens do NOT trigger; the enumerated gotcha tests cover only the acceptor arm ('bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs') and the accept forms.
findings.location: Approach (2) '...denylist ed25519/sha256 etc...' and Testing / AC line 4
scenarios: A future edit to the SHA regex silently drops the denylist and starts flagging legitimate ed25519/sha256 references, with no test to catch the regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the RED/gotcha fixtures to include ed25519- and sha256-bearing comment blocks and assert the detector leaves them clean.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the acceptor id grammar with the repo's short-form convention: specify that a ticket/epic/story/bug id is accepted in its two-group prefix form (e.g. 3006-e198, 4e99-b2ae) as well as the full 4x4 form, so the plan's own prescribed remediations pass the guard.
evidence: Plan: 'ACCEPTED when the block cites a … id — hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…) or word-triple alias'
Plan remediations use 2-group forms: 'classify.py:310 … cite epic 3006-e198', 'cite bug 4e99-b2ae', 'cite bug c7e3-dd16', 'cite 454a-9266', 'story a130-2b7c'
CHANGELOG.md:1135 '… (8dc0-799f)' resolves to ticket 8dc0-799f-3754-46fe — 2-group prefix is the live citation convention
Ticket ids are canonically 4-group hex quads (e.g. 4e99-b2ae-1791-4760, a130-2b7c-429c-43d1)
findings.finding: The acceptor's id grammar ('hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…)') does not match the two-group short-form ticket citations the plan's own remediations prescribe ('epic 3006-e198', 'bug 4e99-b2ae', 'c7e3-dd16', '454a-9266', 'a130-2b7c'), which is also the repo's established convention (CHANGELOG.md:1135 cites '8dc0-799f' → resolves to 8dc0-799f-3754-46fe). If the acceptor requires all four groups, blocks remediated exactly per this plan will not be accepted and will fail the guard.
findings.location: Approach, acceptor definition ('ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id — hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…)'); AC line 1(a)
scenarios: A remediation cites 'epic 3006-e198' in a block that still contains a trigger; the 4x4-only acceptor does not match the 2-group citation and the guard fails the remediated tree
The zero-suppression AC cannot be met because the plan's own remediation form is unrecognized
findings.suggested_fix: Redefine the acceptor to match >=2 hyphen-joined hex groups (each 4 hex) OR the word-triple alias, and state explicitly that the 2-group prefix (the CHANGELOG/comment convention, e.g. 8dc0-799f) qualifies.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the acceptor validates a word-triple alias: name the word source (e.g. the alias store's vocabulary, or a plain 'three lowercase [a-z]+ tokens hyphen-joined' regex) so 'dictionary word' is not left to the executor.
evidence: 'word-triple alias (three lowercase hyphen-joined dictionary words, e.g. robe-creek-zealot, the store's human alias form)'
No dictionary source / word-list provenance given for 'dictionary word'
findings.finding: The acceptor's word-triple alias rule ('three lowercase hyphen-joined dictionary words, e.g. robe-creek-zealot') does not specify HOW the detector decides a token is a 'dictionary word' — no word list, source, or fallback is named, leaving the executor to invent the validation.
scenarios: Executor must decide whether any three hyphen-joined lowercase words accept, or only those in some canonical alias vocabulary
A false accept (arbitrary foo-bar-baz) or false reject (valid alias with a non-'dictionary' word) depends on this undefined check
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact acceptance regex/vocabulary — e.g. 'matches ^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$ (three lowercase alpha tokens), OR is present in the alias store's human-alias list' — rather than the undefined term 'dictionary words'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the 'etc' in the SHA denylist with the concrete exempt-token list (or a rule for deriving it) so the detector's exemptions are deterministic.
findings.finding: The SHA-like detection denylist is left open-ended ('denylist ed25519/sha256 etc'), deferring which hex-adjacent tokens are exempt to the executor's judgment.
scenarios: Executor must guess which additional crypto/algorithm identifiers to denylist to avoid FPs on legitimate current-state references
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the denylist tokens explicitly (e.g. {ed25519, sha256, sha512, blake2b, secp256k1, ...}) or state the derivation rule, and pin it in the detector unit tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the SHA-like trigger and the id acceptor interact on grouped-hex ticket ids so a cited id (e.g. 4e99-b2ae) is recognized as an ACCEPTED id, not flagged as a rot-prone SHA (e.g. match id-shaped hyphenated hex groups before/instead of the bare-SHA rule).
evidence: Plan: 'rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc)'
Remediation prescribes citing 'bug 4e99-b2ae' — '4e99b2ae' is 8 hex chars, digits+letters, not on the stated denylist
Ticket 4e99-b2ae-1791-4760 confirmed resolvable; short prefix is the intended citation
findings.finding: The trigger heuristic (SHA-like = hex >=7 with digits+letters, denylist ed25519/sha256) and the acceptor are not reconciled: a sanctioned short-form ticket citation such as 'bug 4e99-b2ae' collapses to the 8-hex-char token '4e99b2ae' (digits+letters, not denylisted) and can itself TRIGGER the detector, then fail a 4x4-only acceptor — the remediation trips its own guard.
findings.location: Approach, detector trigger definition ('SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters') vs acceptor
scenarios: A block is remediated to cite 'bug 4e99-b2ae'; the differ-independent SHA heuristic matches the hex token and triggers, and the acceptor (if 4x4-only, or if it treats the token as a SHA rather than an id) does not clear it
False positive on legitimate ticket-id citations across the tree, inflating the census and blocking CI
findings.suggested_fix: Define the id pattern (hyphen-joined 4-hex groups) as taking precedence: a token that parses as a ticket-id citation is never counted as a SHA-like trigger; only bare, non-grouped hex runs feed the SHA heuristic.

findings.finding: The detector scans tests/ tree-wide and the plan mandates 'zero suppressions' + 'post-remediation tree scans clean', but the guard's own unit-test corpus must contain the exact rot-prone tokens it detects (dead SHAs like cf93b2b7ad, run/thread ids, 'bug surfaced', date+incident-verb strings) as RED and gotcha fixtures — the plan specifies no self-exclusion mechanism, so the guard would flag its own test fixtures and cannot be green with zero suppressions.
findings.location: Approach (2) CI guard; Testing; AC line 'CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs, passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions'
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt a sibling-guard self-exclusion: either exclude the detector's own test module path from the scan (as check_config_reads.py scopes to src/rebar), OR ship a reviewed allowlist file with per-file count pins plus EXCLUDED_FILES (as check_criteria_vocabulary.py does), and state explicitly that the detector's fixtures live there — then reconcile the 'zero suppressions' wording to mean 'zero suppressions in remediation-scope source', not the fixture corpus.
